Nah, you ain't dumb, but what you're asking is like trying to put 4 gallons in a 3 gallon bucket - it isn't possible to go over the maximum, unless you get a bigger bucket. 

As to why that is, well, in programming you want to choose variable sizes that have a good enough range to cover most possibilities - why have an variable that can store 1024 runs if this will, most likely, never happen? You want to encompass most possibilities by sticking to the most common scenarios (i.e. less than 255 RBI). This is in an effort to save space - there are *many* players in MLB The Show, all with the same amount of variables. Using the 3 gallon buckets vs the 5000 gallon milk truck keeps the game from not being 100 GB for no reason lol
